aimTrainer.title: Aim Trainer
aimTrainer.hint: A 3D "flick" mode calibrated to your real Valorant sensitivity. Configure everything here, then launch the session in a fullscreen game window.

modes.flickDesc: One target at a time, hit it as fast as you can. The basics.
modes.gridshotDesc: Several targets at once: chain them with no downtime.
modes.trackingBeginnerDesc: The target moves continuously, slowly and predictably — keep your crosshair on it.
modes.trackingIntermediateDesc: The target moves faster and changes direction more often.
modes.trackingDesc: The target moves fast and erratically — the toughest tier.
modes.reflexDesc: Targets vanish fast: miss one and it counts against you.
modes.microDesc: Tiny, closely spaced targets for fine precision.
modes.orbitDesc: Targets circle around: anticipation and tracking.
modes.peekDesc: A target peeks out from behind cover, left or right, at Valorant's real strafe speed. Only the head counts.
modes.trackingMultiDesc: Two moving targets at once, crosshair held on whichever one you choose to follow.
modes.strafeDesc: The target crosses the screen in a straight line at constant speed, like a real strafe — trains recoil control while on the move.
modes.patrolSlowDesc: A target walking slowly left to right, no shooting — keep your crosshair on it.
modes.patrolDesc: A target walking left to right, no shooting — keep your crosshair on it as long as possible to score.
modes.patrolFastDesc: A target running left to right, no shooting — the most demanding constant-speed tier.
modes.patrolMultiDesc: Speed (and sometimes direction) changes mid-session — no fixed rhythm to anticipate.
modes.switchModeDesc: Several numbered targets: hit them in the order shown. Hitting one out of order counts as a miss, even if you land the shot.
modes.strafeTapDesc: The target drifts and takes several hits before it actually resets — simulates a mid-range spray on a moving target.
modes.precisionDesc: A tiny target, barely visible for as long as it's shown. The hardest combo: aim fine AND fast.
modes.popcornDesc: Several targets pop up and vanish fast, all over the screen — pure reaction under pressure.
modes.snapHoldDesc: A flick isn't enough: you need to stay settled on the target for a short beat for the shot to count — stops lucky flicks that land by accident.

profile.basedOn: Based on {{matches}} ranked matches — {{agents}} distinct agent(s), {{firstBloods}} first blood(s), {{clutches}} clutch situation(s).

duelistImpulsive.title: Impulsive duelist
duelistImpulsive.text: You take the initiative first in most rounds, but bad patches send you off the rails fast. A real aggression engine, as long as you know when to pump the brakes after a losing streak.

clutchFragger.title: Clutch fragger
clutchFragger.text: You open rounds and close out tight situations: a rare combination of aggression and composure late in the round.

entryFragger.title: Entry fragger
entryFragger.text: You're often the first into contact, whether that means opening space for your team or dying first. A demanding role that carries a lot of weight early in the round.

aggressivePolyvalent.title: Versatile fragger
aggressivePolyvalent.text: You play aggressive AND rotate through a lot of different agents — a rare combination of a player who takes the initiative without ever leaning on a single kit.

clutchAllrounder.title: Complete all-rounder
clutchAllrounder.text: Lots of agents, few losing streaks, and solid clutch numbers: the most complete profile tracked here, with no glaring weakness.

quietFlexible.title: Quiet flexible
quietFlexible.text: You switch agents easily and take bad streaks in stride, but you're not the one looking for first contact. A profile that adapts to the team rather than the ego.

versatileTactician.title: Versatile tactician
versatileTactician.text: You move from one agent to another without losing consistency, and you take bad streaks in stride. The flexible profile of a player who adapts to the team.

unstableCloser.title: Unstable but clutch
unstableCloser.text: Your losing streaks snowball easily, but when it really matters (one-versus-multiple), you show up more often than average. An interesting contrast to watch alongside the Tilt module.

inconsistentPlayer.title: Streaky player
inconsistentPlayer.text: Your losing streaks tend to snowball and weigh on your performance. The Tilt module can help you spot the right moment to take a break.

clutchSpecialist.title: Clutch specialist
clutchSpecialist.text: You stick to a small core of agents, but you're dangerous in clutch situations. Focused expertise that pays off exactly when it counts.

closer.title: Closer
closer.text: You might not dominate the start of rounds, but you're clutch: you convert an above-average number of one-versus-multiple situations.

quietSpecialist.title: Quiet specialist
quietSpecialist.text: Few agents played, little first initiative taken — a composed profile that would rather play its hand than force situations.

specialist.title: Specialist
specialist.text: You stick to a small core of agents rather than rotating. Focused expertise, at the cost of a bit of flexibility when a switch is needed.

steadyPillar.title: Steady pillar
steadyPillar.text: You don't look for first contact, but you absorb bad streaks very well. The kind of teammate the squad can count on without thinking twice.

balancedPlayer.title: Balanced player
balancedPlayer.text: Nothing stands out strongly either way for now — a stable profile, with no glaring excess or weakness on the axes tracked.

weakness.title: Points to work on
weakness.none: Nothing to flag for now — your profile is balanced across every tracked axis.

aggression.title: Aggression
aggression.text: You win few first duels. The Aim Trainer's Peek mode trains exactly that: pushing out and engaging fast on a target that appears.

stability.title: Mental stability
stability.text: Your performance often drops after a loss or a death streak. The Aim Trainer's Precision mode trains calm, controlled aim, useful for not tilting.

versatility.title: Versatility
versatility.text: You play a limited pool of agents. The Composition tool lets you explore other roles and prep a backup agent.

clutch.title: Clutch factor
clutch.text: You win few 1-vs-multiple situations. The Aim Trainer's Snap & Hold mode trains snapping onto a target then holding position, useful in clutches.

aim.title: Precision
aim.text: Your headshot percentage is low. The Aim Trainer's Micro mode forces you to hit tiny targets — exactly the aim it takes to land more headshots.

positioning.title: Positioning
positioning.text: You often die in the very first seconds of the round. The Aim Trainer's Reflex mode trains reacting and neutralizing fast as soon as an opponent appears.

welcome.apiKeyHelp: The API key is used to fetch your matches from HenrikDev (the service the app uses to talk to Valorant) — it's free. Here's how:
welcome.apiKeyStep1: Click the button below — it opens the HenrikDev site in your browser.
welcome.apiKeyStep2: Sign in (with your Discord account if asked), then go to "API Keys" in the left menu.
welcome.apiKeyStep3: Click "Generate New Key" and pick the "Basic" type — that's the free one.
welcome.apiKeyStep4: Copy the long code that gets generated, come back here, and paste it into the "HenrikDev API key" field above.

heatmap.title: Heatmap
heatmap.description: Visualize where you die (or get kills) most often on each map, based on all your cached matches.

analyse.timingHint: Lots of early deaths (0-20s) = you take the initiative early (sometimes too much). Lots of late-round deaths = you hold your positions but might get caught out as time runs low.
analyse.distanceHint: Riot doesn't expose missed shots, so a true accuracy figure isn't possible. What's shown here is your duel win rate (your kills vs your deaths) based on the distance to your opponent at the moment of the kill — the best honest proxy available to see if your aim holds up at range. Distance is approximate (based on in-engine units, ≈ 1 unit = 1 cm).
analyse.clutchHint: A clutch is when you're the last teammate alive while at least one opponent is still alive.
